label: Pro 3.0.0
title: The Pro packages as one service
lede: Pro 3.0.0 adds inverse-server: one Docker image that takes withdrawal and cancellation declarations from any shop, keeps them in a tamper-evident ledger, mails the receipt, runs the case inbox, reminds your team before deadlines and watches your pages. A WooCommerce plugin uses it. Nothing from 2.x was removed.

items.title: Start it with environment variables
items.text: The server stores the ledger in a SQLite file in the /data volume. It needs your company name, a sender, a mail server and a sign-in for the inbox. A wrong setting stops the container at start and names the setting.
items.code:
docker run -d --name inverse -p 8080:8080 -v inverse-data:/data \
  -e INVERSE_COMPANY_NAME="Acme GmbH" \
  -e INVERSE_MAIL_FROM="Acme <service@acme.example>" \
  -e INVERSE_SMTP_URL="smtp://user:password@mail.acme.example:587" \
  -e INVERSE_TEAM_EMAIL=recht@acme.example \
  -e INVERSE_INBOX_USER=team -e INVERSE_INBOX_PASSWORD='at-least-12-characters' \
  -e INVERSE_API_KEY="a-key-for-your-monitoring" \
  ghcr.io/weber-development/inverse-server:3

items.title: From declaration to refund, recorded
items.text: Recorded from a real run of the image with a mail server that records messages. The shop posts the declaration, the team finds the case in the inbox API, marks it refunded with a reply to the customer, and the ledger chain is intact. Then somebody edits the database, and the verify endpoint says where.

items.title: Reminders and a watcher
items.text: With a team address set, the server mails a reminder three days, one day and on the day a refund is due, once per case and not for cases that are closed. With pages listed, it checks them for the buttons every six hours and raises an alarm by webhook and mail when one disappears.

items.title: A WooCommerce plugin
items.text: A page with the shortcode [inverse_withdrawal] finds the order by number and e-mail address, or by the link from My Account, lets the customer pick items and sends the declaration from the shop server to your Inverse server. The order gets a note. We ran it against WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.2 in a browser; the forms pass axe-core.
items.code:
Inverse server:     https://widerruf.acme.example
Withdrawal page:    Widerruf   ([inverse_withdrawal])

note: The demo cannot run the server or the shop for you: it needs your own Docker host, a mail server and WordPress. Not verified: real SMTP servers and mail providers, PostgreSQL for the server, the watcher against live pages, load, several server processes on one data folder, pulling the image with a customer account. Shopware and Magento have no plugin. Not legal advice.
